summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a planned exchange of an antibiotic spacer in the left knee due to a chronic prosthetic joint infection. She underwent an uncomplicated arthrotomy and spacer replacement, with intraoperative cultures showing no growth. Postoperatively, she developed mild anemia requiring one unit of packed red blood cells, which she initially declined but later accepted. Her pain was managed with a transition from PCA to oral medications, and she remained afebrile with stable vital signs. Wound healing was satisfactory with minimal drainage, and she was cleared for discharge to home with home health services. She was prescribed heparin for DVT prophylaxis, continued her baseline immunosuppressive and psychiatric medications, and instructed on wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up. Her chronic conditions, including Stage IV CKD, post-transplant status, and cardiomyopathy, remained stable throughout the admission.
